vignette: A 37-year-old man is referred to hospital with a one-month history of fatigue, loss of appetite and weight loss. He has no relevant past medical history and takes no regular medicines.
opening_statement_lay: I've been tired all the time for about a month. I've gone off my food and I've been losing weight.

raw_material.findings: Marked schistocytosis: numerous red cell fragments. Nucleated red cells (about 6 per 100 white cells) with dysplastic features: nuclear fragmentation, megaloblasts and nuclear atypia. Hypersegmented neutrophils, some with more than six lobes.
raw_material.note: Figure 1B's caption says 'hyperfragmented neutrophils'; the Discussion says hypersegmented neutrophils with more than six segments were seen. Recorded as hypersegmented.

raw_material.test: Analyser red cell and platelet histograms
raw_material.findings: Red cell volume histogram: a small additional peak around 10 fL joined to the main population. Impedance platelet histogram: abnormal distribution.
raw_material.note: Sysmex analyser. Filed under the full blood count; the new schistocyte count test (LAB.HAEM.SCHISTOCYTE_COUNT) carries the number.

raw_material.findings: Hypercellular marrow. Marked megaloblastic change throughout erythroid maturation, with fine chromatin evenly distributed through the nucleus. Myeloid series: hypersegmented and giant neutrophils. Erythroid series: irregular nuclei and multinucleated erythroblasts. Megakaryocytes: separated multinucleated forms.
raw_material.note: The article does not date the marrow; it was done before the day-1 decision not to send ADAMTS13, so it is filed on day 0.

final_dx.text: Vitamin B12 deficiency from low dietary intake of animal foods, presenting as pseudo-thrombotic microangiopathy: haemolytic anaemia with massive schistocytosis, thrombocytopenia, a very high LDH, macrocytosis, circulating megaloblasts and a megaloblastic marrow

secondary_findings: Thrombocytopenia and later leucopenia (pancytopenia) from ineffective haematopoiesis, recovering with treatment
Dysplastic marrow features (dyserythropoiesis, dysmegakaryopoiesis) from B12 deficiency, with a normal karyotype: not a myelodysplastic neoplasm
Raised serum iron and ferritin with ineffective erythropoiesis and haemolysis; no iron deficiency
accepted_differential: Haemolytic uraemic syndrome or atypical HUS
Pernicious anaemia (autoimmune cause of B12 deficiency)
Autoimmune haemolytic anaemia or Evans syndrome
red_herrings: dyserythropoiesis and dysmegakaryopoiesis in the marrow
key_discriminators: reticulocytes 44.8 x10^9/L: inadequate response for the degree of haemolysis
megaloblastic nucleated red cells on the reviewed film
normal coagulation apart from a slightly raised D-dimer
negative direct and indirect antiglobulin tests
diet: meat or seafood about once a month
megaloblastic marrow with a normal karyotype
red cell histogram peak around 10 fL (fragments)
ground_truth.treatment_given: Red cell transfusion on day 1 for severe exertional breathlessness, then intramuscular cyanocobalamin from day 1 on suspicion of B12 deficiency (after the marrow). ADAMTS13 activity was considered but not sent; no plasma exchange. Serum B12 76 pg/mL (56 pmol/L) reported on day 4. Cyanocobalamin injections stopped at discharge on day 7; dietary advice to eat meat. Intrinsic factor and parietal cell antibodies were not tested (not covered by national health insurance in Japan).
ground_truth.outcome: Discharged on day 7 with improving symptoms (Hb 88 g/L, platelets 48 x10^9/L, WBC 3.2 x10^9/L, LDH 1353 U/L). Five weeks after presentation (day 35, outside the playable admission): Hb 131 g/L (printed 13.1 g/dL), MCV 91.5 fL, platelets 219 x10^9/L, WBC 10.2 x10^9/L, LDH 211 U/L, B12 277 pmol/L (printed 375 pg/mL); schistocytes gone and analyser histograms normal. The authors attribute the deficiency to diet rather than pernicious anaemia.

must_do.text: Take a diet history, including how often he eats meat, fish, eggs and dairy
Send serum B12 (or active B12) and folate before transfusion or vitamin treatment
Have the blood film reviewed for megaloblastic nucleated red cells and hypersegmented neutrophils, not only schistocytes
Recognise that a high MCV, a poor reticulocyte response, leucopenia and a disproportionately high LDH argue against TTP
Start parenteral B12 replacement promptly once the deficiency is likely and the samples are taken
Look for the cause of the deficiency, including intrinsic factor antibodies for pernicious anaemia
Give dietary advice, or refer to a dietitian, to correct the low intake of animal foods
Follow the blood count, reticulocytes, LDH and potassium to confirm the response to treatment

must_not_do.text: Start plasma exchange or rituximab (or place a central line for plasma exchange) when the picture is explained by the vitamin deficiency
Diagnose a myelodysplastic neoplasm on marrow dysplasia before excluding B12 and folate deficiency
Give folic acid alone without B12
Transfuse platelets in the absence of bleeding while a thrombotic microangiopathy is not excluded

efficient_path: History with a diet question (releases H09) and the neurological review
Full blood count, reticulocytes, haemolysis screen, DAT, renal function and coagulation
Blood film reviewed by a haematopathologist: megaloblastic nucleated red cells and hypersegmented neutrophils as well as fragments
Serum B12 and folate sent before transfusion or treatment; ADAMTS13 stored or sent
Parenteral B12, red cells for symptoms, no plasma exchange; potassium and reticulocytes followed
Cause sought: diet, intrinsic factor and parietal cell antibodies; dietary advice
teaching_points: B12 deficiency can mimic thrombotic microangiopathy (pseudo-TMA), with schistocytes, thrombocytopenia and a very high LDH
Features favouring B12 deficiency over TTP: high MCV, low reticulocytes, leucopenia, very high LDH, megaloblasts on the film
A PLASMIC score in the intermediate range does not settle the question
ADAMTS13 takes days to return; the film and indices, available within hours, can steer away from plasma exchange (the authors did not send it)
Send B12 and folate before treatment: a single injection makes the serum B12 uninterpretable
Analyser red cell and platelet histograms can support the detection of schistocytes and track their clearance

gaps.guidance: Afebrile; resting tachycardia from anaemia; blood pressure normal (no malignant hypertension); SpO2 normal on air.
A few kilograms over the month; eating less because of poor appetite, no dysphagia or vomiting.
None. The examination is normal, so no paraesthesia or gait disturbance.
No bleeding or bruising; no fever; no confusion or focal symptoms. Do not add features of TTP the article does not report.
None seen.
Urine may be darker than usual; dipstick urobilinogen raised, no protein, no blood, bilirubin negative.
Possibly a sore or smooth tongue; no diarrhoea or dyspepsia; no melaena.

gaps.guidance: Light or no alcohol; ordinary office-type work; lives independently. No reason reported for eating little meat (preference).

gaps.item: Family history (pernicious anaemia, thyroid or autoimmune disease, blood disorders)
gaps.guidance: None known.

gaps.item: Electrolytes, liver enzymes, albumin, glucose, urate
gaps.guidance: Electrolytes normal; AST mildly raised more than ALT (haemolysis and ineffective erythropoiesis); albumin normal; glucose normal.

gaps.item: Serum folate and red cell folate
gaps.guidance: Normal.
Not sent in the article. Curator's decision: activity 64% (normal), reported after the catalogue's three-day turnaround.

gaps.item: Intrinsic factor and gastric parietal cell antibodies
gaps.guidance: Not done in the article (not covered by insurance in Japan). Curator's decision: both negative, following the authors' dietary conclusion (judgement call).
Both raised (MMA 3.10 umol/L, homocysteine 72.0 umol/L). New catalogue tests LAB.CHEM.MMA and LAB.CHEM.HOMOCYSTEINE.

gaps.item: Red cell count, haematocrit, MCH, MCHC, RDW and white cell differential at presentation
gaps.guidance: Consistent with Hb 6.2 g/dL and MCV 117.4 fL (red cell count about 1.5 x10^12/L from the reticulocyte figures); RDW markedly raised; neutrophils low-normal.
Macro-ovalocytes and marked anisopoikilocytosis; no blasts; platelets reduced without clumping; no spherocytes.

gaps.item: Reticulocytes and blood counts between day 2 and day 6
gaps.guidance: Curator's values for days 1, 2, 4 and 7: transfusion of two units on day 1, reticulocyte response from day 3-4, platelets falling to the day-7 value, potassium dipping on day 4.

gaps.item: Viral screen (HIV, hepatitis B and C)
gaps.guidance: Negative.

gaps.item: Upper GI endoscopy and gastric biopsy (if requested)
gaps.guidance: Not done in the article. Normal or non-specific; no atrophic body gastritis. Case Reviewer to confirm.
No splenomegaly, no mass, no lymphadenopathy; kidneys normal.
Sinus tachycardia; troponin normal.

gaps.item: Bone marrow trephine and iron stain
gaps.guidance: Hypercellular with megaloblastic erythropoiesis; storage iron present or increased; no ring sideroblasts; no infiltrate.
